hook: Gates co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen in 1975 and has since become one of the most widely read public commentators on artificial intelligence's likely effects on work, health, and education. His 2023 essay declaring that the age of AI had begun was among the most widely circulated executive statements on the technology that year.

reading.body:
Bill Gates has become one of the most widely heard voices on AI's consequences for society, with his 2023 declaration that "the age of AI has begun" reaching a mass audience and his 2025 predictions about work restructuring extending that influence into mainstream media.

His commentary frames AI as comparable in historical significance to the microprocessor, personal computer, internet, and mobile phone. This positions AI not as a narrow technical capability but as a general-purpose transformation. Gates speaks about AI's effects on labor, health, and education rather than on the underlying systems that enable AI deployment. His public statements reach audiences beyond technology circles, shaping how non-technical audiences understand AI's timeline and scope.

The data does not cover the accuracy of his predictions, the extent to which his statements have influenced policy or investment, or his specific technical positions on compute scaling or power requirements. It establishes only that he holds a prominent platform and uses it to communicate about AI to the general public.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved in the records is the litigation rather than anything Gates himself controls. Both The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI and Authors Guild v. OpenAI are recorded as in discovery, consolidated into MDL 1:25-md-03143 before Judge Stein, with summary judgment briefing in the Times case closed on April 2, 2026, so further rulings are the next recorded step. On Gates's own account, the open question is whether the mandatory safeguards and legislation he called for in the September 2026 coverage follow from his warnings, and whether his projection of a two or three day work week holds. The records show no case naming Gates personally and no company of his own beyond Microsoft, so the watch items are the MDL and the regulatory response his statements urge.
standing.record: The records add up to a founder's profile attached to a company now central to AI litigation, plus a steady run of commentary. Microsoft appears as the company he founded in Redmond in 1975, and two cases on the site name that company or its AI partner: The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI, in discovery with summary judgment briefing closed in April 2026, and Authors Guild v. OpenAI, a class action in discovery, both consolidated into MDL 1:25-md-03143 before Judge Stein. The 26 news stories naming Gates are dominated by one late September 2026 cluster in which he warns that AI could cause a billion deaths and joins calls for safeguards, including legislation, saying self-regulation is not enough. The pattern running through the record is a founder who no longer holds a Microsoft board seat but whose warnings about AI risk are treated as news, while the company he founded sits inside consolidated copyright litigation.
standing.standing: Bill Gates stands in the artificial intelligence record as a co-founder of Microsoft and as a public commentator rather than an operator of an AI developer. The site's records show Microsoft as the company he founded in 1975, and they show him stepping down from its board in 2020, so his current influence runs through commentary and philanthropy rather than a board seat. His 2023 essay on GatesNotes is recorded as among the most widely circulated executive statements on AI that year, and his 2025 remarks on The Tonight Show projected a work week of two or three days. The latest coverage, from late September 2026, places him at the center of calls for AI safeguards and legislation. He is also recorded as co-chair of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

timeline.event: Co-founds Microsoft with Paul Allen on April 4, 1975.
timeline.impact: Starts the company that becomes a dominant force in personal computing software.

timeline.event: Steps down from Microsoft's board of directors on March 13, 2020.
timeline.impact: Ends his formal governance role at the company, per Microsoft's own announcement.

timeline.event: Publishes The Age of AI has begun on GatesNotes on March 21, 2023.
timeline.impact: Argues that generative AI is as significant as the microprocessor, the PC, the internet, and the mobile phone.

timeline.event: Predicts on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in March 2025 that AI could reduce the standard work week to two or three days within about a decade.
timeline.impact: Extends his public commentary on AI from technology to its effects on labor.
